title: Flatness over a filtered colimit of rings
statement: Let $\mathcal I$ be a small filtered category (for instance a directed set) and $i\mapsto R_i$ a functor from $\mathcal I$ to commutative rings with colimit $R=\varinjlim_iR_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and coprojections $\iota_i:R_i\to R$. Let $\psi:R\to S$ be a ring map of commutative rings such that for every object $i$ the composite $\psi\circ\iota_i:R_i\to S$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Then $\psi$ is flat.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05UU (lemma-colimit-rings-flat, line 8857), part (1) with $M=S$ (stated for a directed set; the proof uses only that $\otimes$ commutes with colimits and that filtered colimits of modules are exact, Lemma Tag 00DB lemma-directed-colimit-exact; a filtered index category reduces to a directed set by Categories Lemma Tag 0032 categories-lemma-directed-category-system); cited in more-algebra.tex, proof of Lemma Tag 0AGV (line 3142)

proof.text: Apply the equational criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-equational-criterion] to the target ring S as an R-module through ψ. It suffices to trivialize every finite relation ∑ₖ rₖ • xₖ = 0.

By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise], choose stage representatives aₖ of each coefficient rₖ. Filteredness supplies an object j receiving morphisms from all of the finitely many representing objects, including the empty family. Transport aₖ to bₖ in Rⱼ. The coprojection equations give ιⱼ(bₖ) = rₖ.

Regard S as an Rⱼ-module through ψ ∘ ιⱼ. The relation ∑ₖ bₖ • xₖ = 0 is the original relation because ιⱼ(bₖ) = rₖ. This module is flat by hypothesis. The forward equational criterion gives a finite matrix cₖₜ in Rⱼ and elements yₜ in S with xₖ = ∑ₜ cₖₜ • yₜ and ∑ₖ bₖ cₖₜ = 0.

Use the matrix ιⱼ(cₖₜ) over R and the same yₜ. Its action on S is unchanged by the definition of the composite map. Applying the ring homomorphism ιⱼ to ∑ₖ bₖ cₖₜ = 0 yields ∑ₖ rₖ ιⱼ(cₖₜ) = 0. This is a trivialization of the original relation. The backward equational criterion proves flatness.
